text:
Dennis Hildeby did the quiet, necessary work in Columbus. The Tampa Bay goalie, drafted 122nd overall by Toronto in 2022 out of Farjestad Jr., stopped 28 of 29 shots, and our numbers say the chances against him were worth 2.66 expected goals (a measure of shot quality, not just shot count). That means he saved about 1.7 goals more than an average goalie would have, and it is why TBL walked out with a 3-1 win in a game CBJ controlled for long stretches.

Brandon Hagel supplied the finish, and he did it the hard way. His first-period tip-in at 2:57 came on a chance our model gave just a 4% shot at going in. Matthew Knies tied it on a power-play tip-in late in the period, and the game stayed even until the third, when Jake Guentzel put TBL ahead at 1:06 and Hagel added a slap shot at 7:41. Hagel, picked 159th in 2016 and a 102-point junior scorer at Red Deer, finished with two goals and an assist.

CBJ won the attempt count 72 to 54 and the faceoff count 35 to 23, and Jet Greaves was essentially average in goal, stopping 25 of 28. TBL's real edge came in the second period, when it out-chanced CBJ 1.09 to 0.48 in expected goals. Our deserved-to-win figure, the share of simulated replays each team wins, favored TBL at 56%, so the result was fair even if the shot totals suggest otherwise. TBL also blocked 17 shots to CBJ's 6, which helps explain how a team that was out-attempted by 18 still led in chance quality at even strength. The data doesn't give us the standings or streaks, so the larger picture for both clubs will have to wait.
